title: "Module 4 Assessment: Predicting College Graduation Rates"

## Introduction

The [Colleges 2023 dataset](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jmayberr/math133-stat-learning-fall2026/main/Datasets/colleges2023.csv) contains information on graduation rates and institutional characteristics for approximately 1400 US universities, compiled from the [College Scorecard database](https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/). The dataset includes variables such as cost of attendance, financial aid rates, faculty characteristics, student demographics, and retention rates.

Each problem will be graded on a 2-point scale with:

- 2 = solution is fully correct with proper coding and explanations
- 1 = solution is at least half correct with mostly proper coding and explanations  
- 0 = solution is less than half correct

If you submit the assignment before the due date (not the accept until date), I will provide feedback and give you a chance to resubmit.

## Problem 1

Load the dataset and split it into training and testing sets using a 70-30 split. Use `grad_rate_6yr` as your outcome variable and all other variables except `inst_name` as predictors. Fit a full linear model to the training set and discuss any significant predictors. Compute the test RMSE for this model. 

## Problem 2

Using the `leaps` package, perform an exhaustive search of all possible models on the training set. Answer the following:

- How many predictors does the optimal model have according to BIC? Does it change for Cp?
- Which variables are included in each of the optimal models?
- Compute the test RMSE for both optimal models. 

## Problem 3

Fit an optimal lasso model to the training data using 10-fold cross-validation to select $\lambda$. Report:

- The optimal value of $\lambda$
- Which variables have nonzero coefficients in the final model
- The test RMSE

## Problem 4

Fit an optimal ridge model to the training data using 10-fold cross-validation to select $\lambda$. Report:
- The optimal value of $\lambda$
- Which variables have most importance based on the standardized coefficients
- The test RMSE

## Problem 5

Create a summary table comparing the test RMSE for all four models:

| Model | Test RMSE |
|-------|-----------|
| Full OLS (all predictors) | |
| Best OLS (Cp) | |
| Best OLS (BIC) | |
| Lasso | |
| Ridge | |

Which model performed best? Based on your preferred model, which variables appear to be the most important predictors of 6-year graduation rates? Does this make intuitive sense given what you know about higher education?
